title: Enterprise Onboarding: Escalation, Integration, Known Issues, Support Process, Health Checks & QBR Playbook
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard approach to enterprise onboarding and ongoing support. It combines: onboarding milestones, integration checklist, escalation procedures, known issues and workarounds, the support process, and health-check / QBR materials. The goal is to provide Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and SRE with a single, actionable reference to reduce time-to-value and minimize risk during ramp and production operations.

Audience
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs)
- Support Engineers (L1/L2)
- SRE and Runtime engineering owners
- Customer stakeholders (technical leads)

Key Objectives
- Reduce onboarding time from contract signature to production by 30% through checklists and standardized tasks.
- Ensure clear escalation paths with ownership and SLAs to meet enterprise SLAs.
- Provide a living set of known issues and validated workarounds to minimize customer impact.
- Standardize health-checks and QBR artifacts so customer reviews are data-driven.

1) Onboarding Playbook (High-level phases)

Phase 0 - Pre-sales to Handoff (owner: SE / Solutions Engineering)
1. Confirm customer tier (Hosted / Dedicated / Private) and any regulatory constraints (VPC, on-prem, KMS).
2. Exchange architecture questionnaire and collect network/IP allowlists, SSO metadata, and data residency requirements.
3. Create customer Confluence folder and Slack channel (redwood-customer-<customer-short>) and invite stakeholders.

Phase 1 - Kickoff & Integration (owner: CSM + SE) - 0-2 weeks
- Kickoff agenda: introductions, success criteria, timelines, primary contacts, escalation matrix.
- Integration checklist (minimum):
  - API keys and environment setup (dev/test/prod)
  - VPC peering or VPN (if Private) - validate routing and firewall rules
  - SSO/SAML or OIDC configuration and test account
  - Ingest sample workload and run baseline perf tests (p50/p95 latency, throughput)
  - Baseline cost estimate for projected QPS and token counts
- Deliverable: Integration sign-off doc with sample traffic report.

Phase 2 - Ramp & Validation (owner: CSM + SRE) - 2-8 weeks
- Load testing plan and canary rollout steps (if dedicated/private).
- Validate telemetry: request/response tracing, token-level cost attribution, per-route dashboards.
- Run security review and compliance checklist.
- Establish SLOs (example targets): availability >= 99.95%, p95 latency <= 500ms for standard gen routes.

Phase 3 - Production & QBR cadence (owner: CSM + account exec)
- Go-live checklist: monitoring enabled, alerting thresholds configured, runbooks shared, on-call contacts listed.
- Schedule initial 30/60/90 day health checks and establish QBR cadence (quarterly by default).

2) Integration Guide (detailed checklist and common commands)

Standard API integration steps
- Create API key in Console: Admin > API Keys > Create (role: integration or read-only).
- Example curl call: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"Hello"}'
- Enable streaming in customer settings for low-latency UX.

Network & VPC checklist (Private/Dedicated)
- IP ranges to allow: 34.120.0.0/14, 52.14.0.0/16 (replace with region-specific blocks).
- Ensure inbound HTTPS (443) from customer NAT to control-plane endpoints; outbound access for telemetry to S3-compatible endpoints if required.
- Validate MTU, DNS resolution, and NAT gateway egress rules.

Security integrations
- SAML/SSO: exchange metadata XML, verify NameID and groups mapping.
- KMS: provide key ARN and test encryption/decryption on a sample object.

3) Escalation Playbook (severity matrix & contacts)

Severity definitions and target response times
- Sev 1 (P1): Production outage (all requests failing or latency>10x SLO) - Response: 15 min, Owner: SRE oncall + CS lead
- Sev 2 (P2): Degraded production (partial failure, high error rate or degraded p95) - Response: 60 min, Owner: Runtime engineering + CS
- Sev 3 (P3): Functional issue with workaround, not service impacting - Response: 4 hours, Owner: Support L2
- Sev 4 (P4): Documentation/feature request or minor issue - Response: 2 business days, Owner: Support L1 / Product

Escalation contacts (template)
- Support (L1): support@redwood.ai, Slack: #support-shift
- Support (L2): support-l2@redwood.ai, PagerDuty: PDL-Redwood-Support
- Runtime/SRE oncall: pagerduty-sre@redwood.ai, Slack: #sre-oncall
- Customer Success lead: cs-<customer>-lead@redwood.ai

Escalation steps (numbered)
1. Triage in support ticketing system (Zendesk): collect logs, request IDs, timestamps, and client configuration.
2. Reproduce issue in sandbox or staging. If reproducible and severity >= P2, page SRE.
3. SRE invokes runbook for impacted service; if rollback required, follow dedicated rollback playbook.
4. Notify customer point-of-contact with status updates every 30 minutes for P1, hourly for P2.
5. After remediation, create post-incident summary and assign postmortem owner if impact >= 1 hour or customer SLA breach.

4) Known Issues & Workarounds (living table)

Common issues (current as of last_updated):
- ISSUE-2026-014 | Symptom: Streaming responses stall after ~30s for long-lived websockets. | Workaround: Enable chunked-transfer or increase keepalive TTL to 60s; for Private deployments, ensure load balancer idle timeout >= 120s. | Status: workaround validated
- ISSUE-2025-209 | Symptom: Occasional tokenization mismatch when using custom tokenizers. | Workaround: Use Redwood tokenizer endpoint to canonicalize inputs prior to send. | Status: monitoring
- ISSUE-2026-030 | Symptom: Cost attribution missing for some routed fallback requests. | Workaround: Tag routes with explicit model_version label; enable per-request metadata. | Status: in progress (runtime patch scheduled)

Process for adding known issues
1. Support or SE files a Known Issue ticket in the internal tracker with reproduction steps and customer impact.
2. SE/Runtime assigns priority and adds to the confluence known-issues table.
3. For high-impact issues, schedule a mitigation or rollback and update customers via CS.

5) Support Process (ticket lifecycle & SLAs)

Ticket lifecycle
- Intake: automated creation from email, console support button, or partner integrations.
- Triage: L1 support validates and classifies severity, collects logs, and attempts known workarounds.
- Escalate: if not resolved within severity SLA, escalate to L2 or SRE.
- Resolve & close: verify fix with customer, publish workaround if needed, and tag ticket with root cause.
- Postmortem: for Sev1 incidents or repeat customer impact, owner prepares incident review.

SLA examples (internal):
- Initial response: P1=15m, P2=60m, P3=4h, P4=2bd
- Resolution targets: P1=4h, P2=24h, P3=7bd, P4=30bd (target varies by contract)

Support tooling and artifacts to collect
- Required attachments: request_id, timestamp, region, model_version, sample payloads, and token accounting evidence.
- Telemetry links: per-route dashboard, traces link, and error logs (include presigned links if needed).

6) Health Checks & QBR Materials (metrics, dashboards, agendas)

Standard health-check runbook (30/60/90-day and ongoing)
- Key metrics to review:
  - Availability (rolling 30d) - target >= 99.95%
  - Error-rate (4xx/5xx) - target < 0.5%
  - Latency p50/p95/p99 for primary routes
  - Tokenized cost per 1M tokens and monthly spend variance vs forecast
  - Throughput (requests/sec) and concurrency distribution
  - Cache hit rate for prefix/KV caching (if enabled)
- Dashboard links: include per-model and per-route dashboards.
- Action items for health checks: scaling recommendations, batching/quantization suggestions, and fallback policy adjustments.

QBR agenda (quarterly)
1. Business context and success metrics (customer presentation)
2. Usage trends and cost breakdown (token-level)
3. Reliability review (SLOs, incidents, and remediation)
4. Performance optimization opportunities (batching, quantization, model variant)
5. Roadmap items and upcoming deprecations/compatibility notices
6. Action plan / owners and next steps

QBR deliverables
- Executive summary slide (1 page)
- Detailed metrics workbook (CSV) with raw telemetry for the quarter
- Action register with owners and deadlines

7) Ownership, Running this Playbook, and Escalation Drills

RACI (owner callouts)
- CS Lead: organizes kickoffs and QBRs.
- SE: handles integration and initial performance validation.
- Support: triage and first-line remediation.
- SRE/Runtime: escalations for availability/perf incidents and runbook maintenance.

Drills and game-days
- Schedule annual escalation drills with customers for Dedicated/Private fleets.
- Run internal SRE game-days each quarter to validate runbooks and oncall paging.

Appendices
A. Templates
- Kickoff agenda template (copy to customer folder)
- Integration sign-off checklist (checklist CSV)
- Incident postmortem template

B. Example Alerts and Thresholds
- Route-error-rate > 0.5% for 5m -> P2 alert to support-l2 + SRE oncall
- p95 latency > 2x baseline for 10m -> PagerDuty to SRE

C. Change log
- 2026-02-15: Initial published version (Maya Thompson)
- 2026-03-04: Updated known issues and added QBR deliverables (Maya Thompson)

If you have additions or discover a new recurring issue, please file a ticket and nominate a reviewer so we can keep this playbook current.
